Beyond the cash rewards and iPhones presented to Nigeria’s victorious Flamingos during a dinner at the Lagos House, Marina on Sunday, Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu had a bigger message for the players on their historic FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup triumph in Morocco. Speaking while receiving the team in Lagos, the governor urged the players to remain focused, disciplined and consistent, warning that sustaining success would require even greater commitment as they progress through the ranks. “At this stage, you have not yet reached the height of your careers. You have to tell yourselves that you are just starting. This is the first stage, and you have to work even harder because many of your other friends who didn’t make the team will also begin to train harder. “By the time you move to the U-20 level, they will want to be in the team, and you know they are also good players. They will come hard. Getting to the top might not be so difficult, but sustaining that level requires consistency. My prayer for you is that you get to the Super Falcons and reach the levels of players like Asisat Oshoala and Rasheedat Ajibade,” Sanwo-Olu said. The governor also praised head coach Akeem Busari and his technical crew, crediting their guidance, encouragement and emphasis on discipline for the team’s historic achievement. They look up to you, and they still go back to you. When all of us are not there, you are the one who keeps talking to them and encouraging them to maintain discipline, mentally and physically. “If we go and win a World Cup, it is not by chance. You saw the Brazilians and Japanese; they were crying. So, I thank you, coach, and your entire crew for pushing them and telling them they could do it. Now, they are the pride of the nation,” he said. Sanwo-Olu further acknowledged how the Flamingos’ performances gradually won over Nigerians, particularly after the disappointments involving the country’s senior national teams had initially dampened expectations. “Like the MC said, we were not all watching because of the disappointments with the senior teams. When they said they were going to the World Cup, everyone said, ‘Okay.’ But by the time it got to the quarter-finals, everyone was paying attention. Everybody identifies with success. “But a lot of people will not know the journey you have been through, the discipline, commitment and dedication, and the fact that each time you fall down, you get up very quickly,” the governor said. He described sports as an important tool for personal development, noting that its benefits extend beyond financial rewards to include intellectual, psychological and mental growth. “Sports is one of the strongest social enablers, not even financially. It helps to activate the brain, stimulate cognitive abilities and develop someone psychologically and mentally. You are on a journey that everyone wishes they could go on, and you are starting yours on a very commendable note. “Keep your heads together. Don’t think that you have reached the heights and begin to miss it. Stay together, remain focused. Stay in school, stay at your clubs and remain disciplined. What they say you should stay off, stay off it. Make sure you are dedicated to developing yourselves. I can assure you that you will get there once you have that self-determination, and it doesn’t matter where you are from,” he added. Sanwo-Olu also pledged to keep track of the players’ progress, stressing that Lagos State would remain interested in their development beyond the reception and rewards. “Personally, I will be monitoring you because you cannot fall our hands. So, we will be monitoring you because it is important to us that you do well,” he said. The governor concluded by acknowledging the contributions of the players from Lagos while emphasising that the reception was organised to celebrate the entire team, regardless of their state of origin. “I don’t want to talk about the ones that came from Lagos. You know yourselves, and I know you. You know that my heart is there. All of you have won today for your team, and it is the team that we are celebrating and honouring. “So, for all of us in Lagos, we feel truly honoured that your coach and entire staff, the NFF and the National Sports Commission agreed with us to honour you,” he said.
